subject: Follow-up: Model evals & multilingual quality checks (EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hofmann <lena.hofmann@globexretail.com>, Oliver Meier <oliver.meier@globexretail.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual evals)

Hi Lena / Oliver,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about Globex's roadmap for localized search and customer-facing assistance. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goal: validate model quality for EU languages (DE/FR/ES) and APAC (JA/KO) for the search+answer use case and short-form generation (product blurbs).
2) Success criteria: intent accuracy > 92% in DE/FR/ES and human-quality score within 10% of EN baseline for JA/KO on our evaluation rubric.
3) Initial plan (what Redwood will deliver):
   - curated prompt set (attached: multilingual_prompt_set_v2.csv) covering the above locales
   - model recommendations and a lightweight benchmark report with token/latency cost estimates
   - run 3 experimental evals: a baseline large float model, a 8-13B quantized variant, and a tuned instruction-lite variant to check regressions

Next steps I propose:
- Globex to confirm scope (DE/FR/ES + JA/KO) and whether you can share a small sample of in-domain prompts/content (anonymized) by Apr 16.
- Redwood to run the first pass evals and share a draft report + recording the week of Apr 19.
- Schedule a 30-min sync (tech + procurement) on Apr 22 to go over results and procurement questions.

I've cc'd Jonas (ML) to help with model selection and Dylan (Solutions) — he can jump in on integration/latency questions once we have the sample data. I'll attach the prompt set and the initial eval plan.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: multilingual_prompt_set_v2.csv

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — this looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Scope: yes, please include DE/FR/ES and JA/KO. For JA/KO we have less labeled data, so a small synthetic set is fine for the first pass.
- Data residency / privacy: for EU languages we need to confirm that any evaluation artifacts remain in-region and that no customer PII is persisted outside of Globex controls. Do you have SOC 2 / data residency docs you can share?
- Procurement: Oliver will handle procurement and will need an estimated monthly spend range and licensing terms for both hosted and dedicated options.

We can share an anonymized sample of 300 prompts by end of day Apr 16. Please include any guidance on the format.

Best,
Lena
Head of Search, Globex Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hofmann <lena.hofmann@globexretail.com>, Oliver Meier <oliver.meier@globexretail.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual evals)

Hi Lena / Oliver — appreciate the quick reply. A few concrete items to address your asks:

1) SOC2 / Data residency: attached is our SOC2 summary and the compliance package (soc2_compliance_package.pdf). For the hosted evals we can ensure EU-region compute and data retention controls; for Dedicated/Private we can provide air-gapped / VPC options — happy to have our security team sign an NDA and provide an overlay for procurement.

2) Model recommendations (initial):
   - strong baseline: redwood/gptx-13b-fp16 (best quality-to-latency tradeoff for DE/FR/ES)
   - cost-efficient candidate: open-quant-13b-8bit (comparable semantic accuracy on retrieval-augmented tasks after our suggested prompt tuning)
   - low-latency option for production: redwood/fast-8b-quant (suitable for JA/KO short-form where tokenization differences matter)

We will run the following experiments: (A) full-fp16 inference for baseline, (B) 8-bit quantized model eval, (C) instruction-tuned small variant to detect regressions vs. baseline. We'll produce per-locale precision/recall, latency metrics (p95), and a human-eval summary.

3) Costs: rough back-of-envelope for the evaluation run (estimates only):
   - Baseline eval pass (all locales): ~$2,500 in hosted compute (short-turn);
   - Full benchmarking + human eval: ~$8k - $12k depending on annotation scope;
   - Production monthly ranges (hosted): from low thousands to high depending on QPS; we'll provide a tailored estimate once we know expected throughput.

4) Attachments and links:
   - multilingual_prompt_set_v2.csv (attached)
   - globex_initial_eval_plan.xlsx (attached)
   - SOC2 package attached; full docs are available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-globex-evals

5) Next meeting: thanks for proposing Apr 22. I've added a 30-min placeholder on Apr 22 09:00 CEST — please confirm/adjust.

Action items I've assigned:
 - Globex: share anonymized sample by Apr 16 (Lena)
 - Redwood: run first-pass evals and share draft report week of Apr 19 (Marissa / Jonas)
 - Redwood: provide procurement estimate for hosted and dedicated options (Marissa)

Looping in Jonas and Dylan for the experimental design and to call out any locale-specific tokenization or quality risks (esp. Japanese segmentation and Korean honorifics).

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: globex_initial_eval_plan.xlsx, soc2_compliance_package.pdf
